title: Odysseus Lands — Tilted!
description: IM-1 touched down at Malapert A but came to rest on its side. A landing leg caught on the surface. Most instruments still collected data despite the tilt.

title: First Lunar Sunset for IM-1
description: As the Sun set over Malapert A, Odysseus powered down. The tilted lander's solar panels lost their last light.

title: Retroreflector Still Works!
description: Even on its side, the Laser Retroreflector Array is passive — no power needed. It will bounce laser light back for decades.

title: Peregrine: Propellant Leak
description: Hours after launch, Astrobotic's Peregrine developed a propellant leak. The lander could not attempt a lunar landing. All 5 NASA payloads gathered what data they could during transit.

title: Blue Ghost 1 Lands Successfully!
description: Firefly's Blue Ghost 1 became the first fully successful CLPS mission, delivering 10 NASA payloads to Mare Crisium.

title: Blue Ghost Photographs Lunar Sunset
description: SCALPSS 1.1 cameras captured a stunning sequence of the Sun setting behind the rim of Mare Crisium — real footage from the lunar surface.

title: LISTER Drills Into the Moon
description: The heat-flow probe began drilling into the regolith at Mare Crisium to measure how heat escapes from the Moon's interior.

title: Athena Launches for the South Pole
description: IM-2 lifted off carrying MSolo and a Micro-Nova hopper to the Shackleton Connecting Ridge — one of the most extreme landing sites ever attempted.

title: Athena Lands Near Shackleton
description: IM-2 touched down at the lunar south pole. MSolo will search for volatile compounds — water and CO₂ — in one of the coldest places in the solar system.

title: 14 Days of Darkness
description: The lunar night lasts about 14 Earth days. Without sunlight, temperatures plummet below -170°C. Only passive instruments like the retroreflector survive without power.

title: No Signal From the Far Side
description: On the lunar far side, Earth never rises above the horizon. Blue Ghost 2 will carry a relay satellite so instruments can phone home.

title: Lunar Dust Gets Everywhere
description: RAC confirmed that lunar dust clings to surfaces through electrostatic charge. It coats solar panels, clogs mechanisms, and degrades optics over time.
